general.temas: The election campaign dominates the front pages, with attention to the PSOE’s proposals, particularly on housing and care, and to opinion polls and party strategies. The assault on the PP candidate in Hernani and Feijóo’s response also feature repeatedly. Only OKdiario highlights the call for a truckers’ strike before Christmas.
general.motivo_crispacion: The assault on the PP candidate in Hernani and Feijóo’s announcement that he will campaign in Gipuzkoa account for much of the tension. The PP leader asks Sánchez to tell his allies not to use violence during the campaign, while the PSOE condemns the assaults. Some headlines and statements use polarizing language amid the electoral contest. Reports on housing and care proposals, science, cooperative initiatives and other news partly offset that atmosphere.

El País.resumen:
- The election campaign dominates the front page, with PSOE proposals on housing, child-rearing and energy, and coverage of the parties.
- A poll examines shifts among PSOE voters; Junts rules out supporting Sánchez’s re-election.
- Other reports cover campaign podcasts, young first-time voters and Sigüés’s electoral history.
- The migration route to the Canary Islands records 1,500 arrivals in a single day; there are also accounts from victims of banking fraud.
- There are reports on Jensen Huang, the arrest of singer Gabito Ballesteros and the effects of the El Niño climate phenomenon.
El País.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “the drama,” “glory and downfall” and “drives the climate crazy” resort to dramatization, while the quote “good politics and bad manners” presents a simplified contrast.
El País.sesgo: The selection focuses on the election campaign and gives prominent attention to the PSOE, its proposals and its voters, although it also includes information about the PP and Junts. Social and economic issues are approached with a focus on those affected and the risks involved.

El Mundo.resumen:
- The PP and Vox could win up to 199 seats, while the PSOE appears to be stagnating and losing support among former voters.
- Campaign coverage includes proposals from Sánchez and Colau, an interview with a senior PP figure and Feijóo’s reaction to the assault on the PP candidate in Gipuzkoa.
- A police analysis describes the neo-Nazi group Núcleo Nacional and how it radicalizes.
- The front page addresses the control of nuclear weapons and artificial intelligence, as well as the “invisible war against the West.”
- Other topics include unemployment among university graduates and a cooperative supermarket in Madrid.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Alongside informative headlines are expressions such as “cling on,” “steals,” “copies” and “the invisible war against the West,” as well as emotive quotes about distrust of Sánchez.
El Mundo.sesgo: The selection and wording show a critical approach to Sánchez and the PSOE, particularly in highlighting the loss of support and accounts from former voters. Space is also given to proposals from other electoral lists and to a senior PP figure.

ABC.resumen:
- The election campaign is the focus of the front page, with proposals from Sánchez and an event announced by Feijóo in Gipuzkoa.
- Several news stories report criticism or comments about Begoña Gómez’s presence on the campaign trail and relations with Morocco.
- The coverage examines Aragón’s value as an electoral bellwether and consular appointments to process applications for Spanish citizenship.
- The front page includes news about astronomy, Azúcar Moreno, Cristiano Ronaldo and a new Suzuki model.
- Infanta Margarita remains hospitalized in Madrid with an infection.
ABC.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although eye-catching expressions appear, such as “our rail network is falling apart” and “Portugal’s coach mocks Cristiano.”
ABC.sesgo: The selection gives considerable prominence to the election campaign and includes several criticisms of Sánchez and his government, alongside his proposals. The approach is partly critical of the government, but the news presented does not establish an unequivocal partisan orientation.

Público.resumen:
- Gabriel Rufián warns about fascism and questions the unity of the left.
- Sánchez proposes enshrining protections for pensions and abortion in the Constitution and raising taxes on large property owners; Frente Amplio proposes care leave for “chosen family.”
- Several articles address electoral divisions, the left’s options and the security of the vote.
- A news story reviews the merger of the Galician savings banks and their public bailout of more than 9 billion euros.
- The front page includes political profiles, an interview with Mauro Entrialgo and a report on voting in Barakaldo.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “suck on fascism,” “friends of genocidal killers” and “the inquisitor who found witches” resort to confrontation and disparagement, although other headlines are descriptive.
Público.sesgo: The selection pays particular attention to the proposals and strategies of the left and includes statements sharply critical of the right. Some headlines use disparaging language, while others are primarily informative.

OKdiario.resumen:
- Rafa Jódar makes his debut against Zverev at the ATP Finals.
- Sánchez promises to create a “friendship union” in the Civil Code.
- The PP responds to assaults suffered by young party members in Hernani; Feijóo announces that he will campaign in Gipuzkoa.
- Switzerland improves a climate model and Europe tightens requirements for financing cars.
- CCOO calls a truckers’ strike; news about education, animals, psychology and celebrities also features prominently.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly informative, although expressions such as “stands up to” and some celebrity headlines resort to confrontation or emotional appeal.
OKdiario.sesgo: The political selection pays attention both to a promise by Sánchez and to the PP’s responses to the assaults in Hernani. The text of the latter story uses disparaging expressions such as “the ETA member’s cubs.”

opiniones.comunista:
I see a campaign that should be debated in terms of class: who can live off their work and who earns income from basic necessities. The Socialist proposal to devote 1% of GDP to social housing is a step in the right direction, but taxing large property owners more is not enough: we need a permanent stock of public housing and forms of collective ownership that take housing out of the realm of speculation.

The news about the bailout of the Galician savings banks brings another question to mind: if public money is mobilized to save financial institutions, why not advocate for public banking that responds to social needs? I also think it is right to recognize care between people who are not related, provided that leave is genuinely accessible to working people.

In the face of the power of big capital, I stand for strong public services and rights that do not depend on the ability to pay.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I see a campaign that promises to solve from above the problems we experience down below. Social housing and care leave can ease real needs, but I resist the idea that access to a home or recognition of our relationships should depend on the will of political parties and the bureaucracy of the state. I want communities capable of deciding on and managing their resources together, without owners who concentrate power or authorities who speak in our name.

The cooperative supermarket La Osa offers a different picture: people contributing their labor to sustain a shared project. It is not a magic solution, but it shows that we can organize without waiting for orders. And I reject the assaults in Hernani: collective freedom requires that no one be driven out of public space for thinking differently.
opiniones.liberal:
Housing and child-rearing deserve attention, but I do not believe the answer is to turn every need into a new spending promise. Devoting 1% of GDP to social housing and raising taxes on large property owners may sound appealing; it also requires asking who will foot the bill and what will happen to incentives to invest. I would rather make construction easier, reduce red tape and lower taxes so that families have more resources and can make their own decisions. Solidarity is necessary, but it is no substitute for personal responsibility, nor does it justify a state without limits.

The assault on the PP candidate in Hernani deserves unequivocal condemnation. Political freedom includes campaigning without intimidation, whatever the party. A limited state must carry out that essential task firmly: protecting everyone’s rights.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
The arrival of 1,500 people in the Canary Islands in a single day demands more than emergency resources. We must treat those who arrive humanely, but also regain effective control of the borders, combat irregular migration routes and enforce the law. A nation that does not decide who enters gives up an essential part of its sovereignty.

I am also concerned that the campaign is turning into a spectacle while crucial issues are being debated. The assault in Hernani is intolerable: defending political freedom means ensuring that everyone can campaign without intimidation. And, when it comes to promises on housing and child-rearing, I want fewer announcements and more clarity about their costs and results. Supporting families and helping them secure a home must be a national priority, not an election slogan. Traditions and family ties deserve protection, not to be treated as a relic.
opiniones.centro:
The assault on the PP candidate in Hernani deserves unequivocal condemnation. No one should encounter stones or intimidation where there should be democratic debate. I welcome the condemnation of the assault and believe that all parties must defend their opponents’ right to campaign, without electoral calculations.

I also think it is right to put housing and child-rearing at the center of the debate. But devoting 1% of GDP to social housing requires an explanation of how it will be financed, where it will be built and how the results will be evaluated. Announcing taxes on large property owners is not enough: we need to increase supply, mobilize private investment and protect those who cannot gain access to a home. I would rather see a lasting agreement among government bodies and parties than a promise that changes with every legislative term. Social ambition gains strength when accompanied by rigor.
